cases.name: Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc.
UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc.

profile_text.body:
Suno is a for-profit startup founded in 2022 and headquartered in Cambridge, Massachusetts. Its site describes it as an AI music generator that builds complete songs with vocals, lyrics, and production from a single text prompt in under a minute, across genres, and also offers instrumentals and beat making. The company describes Suno Studio as a first-of-its-kind web-based generative audio workstation that combines traditional DAW functionality with AI-powered music creation. Paid tiers are described on the site: the Pro plan gives 500 songs a month, access to v5.5, commercial use rights, priority generation, the Song Editor, stem separation into vocal and instrument stems, and audio uploads of up to 8 minutes; the Premier plan gives 2,000 songs a month, Suno Studio, a multitrack editor, MIDI export, Persona Voices, and early access to new features.

The site markets the product as the market-leading AI song generator and the number one AI music generator, and says millions of people use it for fun, content, and professional projects. Suno is tracked as a Voice and Audio product, with music generation and IP provenance noted as the relevant themes.

The litigation record lists eight cases involving the company. UMG Recordings, Sony Music et al. v. Suno, Inc. is in the U.S. District Court for the District of Massachusetts, where Rugnetta v. Suno, Inc., Pilavian v. Suno, Inc., Reyna v. Suno, Inc., and S.A. Jamendo v. Suno Inc. are also filed. Gawronski v. Suno Inc. is in the District Court for the Southern District of Texas, Poseidon Wave Media LLC v. Suno, Inc. is in the Southern District of New York, and Woulard v. Suno, Inc. is in the Northern District of Illinois. Massachusetts accounts for 176 in the law exposure record.
